slides.say: The operation diamond is defined for every even integer x that's zero or more. Diamond of x is two when x is zero, and nine minus diamond of x minus two when x is two or more. Diamond of six is equal to what?

This is a circular rule. The diamond appears inside its own definition, so it keeps calling itself. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, going down to the start value and back up, and then with the pattern.

[short pause] Six is two or more, so we use the second rule. Diamond of six is nine minus diamond of six minus two, which is diamond of four. But we don't know diamond of four yet, so we keep going down.

Now we climb back up. Diamond of two is nine minus two, which is seven. Diamond of four is nine minus seven, which is two. And diamond of six is nine minus two, which is seven. Choice number four is our answer.
